Published online:
September 9, 2025

Geographic focus:
Europe (EU), Italy, Germany, China; with secondary mentions of Morocco, Turkey

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references 2024 EU tariff measures, H1 2025 export data, Volkswagen restructuring
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ~10% export drop expected for full year 2025, Volkswagen overhaul near-term fallout
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — 40–50% drop in Italian auto parts exports by 2028, broader EU automotive industry shakeout

Synopsis:
The head of Italian auto suppliers lobby Anfia is calling for the EU to impose 80% tariffs on Chinese vehicles and components above a threshold of 8% of annual EU registrations. The article highlights mounting pressure on European — particularly Italian and German — automotive supply chains from Chinese competition. Italian suppliers exported €4.9bn to Germany in 2025, with Volkswagen alone representing up to 20% of that. Exports are already declining and could collapse 40–50% by 2028 without stronger protective measures. The lobby chief also criticises the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act as ineffective and questions whether Chinese OEMs building European factories will source locally, labelling them "screwdriver factories."
